newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to start arabica coffee project in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to start arabica coffee project in 1997.

text.p: Vietnam will start work on a project next year to grow and process up to 70,000 hectares (173,000 acres) of arabica beans, the vice-director of the national Coffee Research Institute said on Thursday.
Hoang Thanh Tiem, speaking by telephone from the coffee-growing region of Dak Lak, told Reuters that the project would be funded by a concessional loan from France.
The Vietnam Economic Times journal said the cost of the project, which will be carried out in the hills of Vietnam's central provinces, was around $42 million.
Vietnam currently has some 200,000 hectares (494,000 acres) of coffee under cultivation and, with annual output of around 230,000 tonnes, it is Asia's second-largest producer after Indonesia.
But just 1.5 percent of its crop is arabica, a more precious variety used in gourmet brews and usually grown in South America.
